<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Numbers (plans, PRDs, roadmaps, blueprints, migrations) are handed out by hand today: pm-001 checks folders and branches and logs claims in a markdown LOG, and harness builder only sees local worktrees. Requirement and step states lag the code because nobody records delivery at merge. This plan adds a store-backed claim verb and a merge-time delivery verb. Per ruling C23, delivery is a verb the merger runs once (no poll, no webhook), and pij never pushes: it prints the `ddocs set` edits that fill `delivered_by`, and the PM puts them in its next docs PR.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- Two seats claiming the same kind at once always get different numbers, and every claim names its seat.
- A claim is released when its work merges or its seat closes.
- After a merge, one command records what the PR delivered and tells the owning PM, without any polling.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- Editing the project docs from the daemon: pij prints the edits and never commits or pushes them (C23).
- A GitHub webhook or any periodic check of PR state.
- Changing how plans are scaffolded (harness plan new keeps its --ordinal flag; the claim supplies the number).

## Research Context

Code facts (2026-11-04, main 6ccd4d8): no GitHub API, webhook or merge hook anywhere; the daemon never calls gh (reqwest is a dependency but unused for PRs). No project-scoped counter exists; streams.ordinal (crates/store/src/orchestration.rs:412-439) shows the reserve-under-BEGIN-IMMEDIATE pattern with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; begin_write is crates/store/src/migrate.rs:267-268. Seat card: POST /v1/state -> seat_state (crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:636, 2682); report handler at mod.rs:3563. Tombstone: publish_tombstone in crates/store/src/registry.rs:48-99 (close, reap and revive all pass through it). Schemas: pij/prd requirement rows have optional `delivered_by` (.dd/schemas/pij/prd/schema.json:143-183); roadmap steps have state, plan and delivers (.dd/schemas/pij/roadmap/schema.json:66-118). Latest migration 0031; 0032 is claimed by plan 195, 0033 by this plan.

<a id="risks"></a>

## Risks

| risk | likelihood | impact | mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A PR body without a `Delivers:` line records nothing and nobody notices. | Medium | Medium | `pij delivered` refuses by name when the line is missing, and the PR template carries it (AC7). |
| gh missing or unauthenticated on the merger's machine. | Medium | Low | Named refusal with the install or auth step; doctor reports the gh pij will use. |
| Numbers used by work in flight before claims existed collide with the first claims. | Low | Medium | The main-checkout scan plus pm-001 importing today's LOG claims (plans 190 to 196, migrations 0031 to 0033) with `pij claim` at first use. |

<a id="execution-guardrails"></a>

## Execution Guardrails

- Tests use a private daemon, a scratch store and a fake gh; never the prod daemon or a real PR.
- Builds scoped with -p; check `df -h /System/Volumes/Data` first; stop and tell pm-001 under 25 GB.
- No `git add -A`, no `--no-verify`, never push refs/notes/*. No node_modules: TS proof is CI on the exact head.
- One push per review round; no pushes after a PR is out for verdicts unless a verdict asks.
